title: Allium Cepa
text: A remedy for acute catarrh, with increased secretions from the nose and eyes. It is indicated in cases of hay-fever and common cold. The characteristic symptom is a profuse, acrid nasal discharge and a profuse, bland lacrimation. There is a general feeling of heat and burning. Confused. Forgetful. Fears that the pain will become unbearable. Headache, especially in the forehead. Vertigo. Profuse, bland lacrimation. Eyes red and burning. Photophobia. Profuse, acrid nasal discharge, which excoriates the upper lip and nose. Sneezing. Sensation of a lump in the nose. Sensation of a splinter in the throat. Hoarseness. Hawking of mucus. Appetite poor. Thirst. Burning in the stomach. Distended with gas. Rumbling. Sharp pains. Violent cough, with a sensation of tearing in the larynx. Hoarseness. Shortness of breath. Aching and lameness in the limbs. Neuralgic pains in the fingers. Worse in a warm room and in the evening. Better in the open air. Compare: Euphrasia; Pulsatilla; Arsenicum album. Third to thirtieth potency.
